label: paragraph_title
text: Backward Hongkong

label: paragraph_title
text: [To the 12/1/2007 at the China Mail]

label: text
text: Sir, — Last Saturday I wanted to go to the Government School Sports at "Cheung Chau". I had not the slightest objection to spending a night or even the weekend there for the memory of happy times spent at Cheung Chau is still with me. The nights provided the house is favourably situated, are cool and the solubility of Cheung Chauites is too well known to need stressing byane. Become it was impossible for me to spend the night there, however, owing to reasons into which I need not enter, I had to give up the idea of going to the sports, the last launch leaving before the sports had hardly got into their swing.

label: text
text: The public to which I want to direct attention; however, is not that I was edged to miss the sports but the lack of enterprise on the part of the Government in not providing, or causing to be provided, facilities for getting out to places. Term suburban, whether they be on land or water, in the development of which lies the solution of many of the housing difficulty. To give another example, if I miss a train at an absurdly early hour I am unable to get out to Fading, Emo or any other off the places which are developing along that route, consequently the inducement for me to take up my permanent abode there is correspondingly less.

label: text
text: The Government is too short sighted in these matters of development. They do not seem to recognize how rapidly the Colony is going forward. Take the Kowloon buses for instance. It was surely not a far-seeing policy for give even in trial to such a system or lack of system as has been tobead for so long and the Government is now having to make namels in this respects.

label: text
text: It is in the hope that it may be led to realise its shortcomings in other respects that I have penned the above lines.

label: paragraph_title
text: Thirst Quencher.

label: text
text: To the Editor of the China Mail.

label: text
text: Sir,—Many of us are more likely to be interested in a cooling drink for summer than in the wearing or otherwise of what your correspondents described as "Cissy Shirts." There must be someone in the Colony who knows what is the right kind of drink for a Hongkong summer. I remember seeing the recipe for a cocktail thirst quencher guaranteed to do its work, but failed "to keep what would have been a valuable source of comfort. If you or any of your readers can suggest a suitable summer drink that meets the "hard" drinker as well as the "soft" he or she will be doing a service to suffering thirsty humanity.

label: paragraph_title
text: Boxing Decision.

label: text
text: (To the Editor of the China Mail)

label: text
text: Sir,—The letter of your correspondent "Candid" is so full of inaccuracies that he is hardly worth consideration. To quote one instance, he says that Dupree won by a street, and in the same breath he says that the margin was small. "Surely these are contradictory. Then again in the details given in the letter he has much to say about Dupree's lefts. These did not worry Cartlidge in the least for all I could see," as after all they amounted to something like an old lady caressing a baby.

label: text
text: The consensus of opinion at the hall was that Cartlidge was the better man on the run of the fight. I was not guided by this when I wrote my impressions on Sunday: If “Candid” had read yesterday’s morning papers the would have seen the opinion expressed that Cartlidge was clearly the winner.

label: text
text: Not being a Peimanist, I have made no mental calculations, and I still adhere to the belief that the decision should have gone to Cartlidge.

label: paragraph_title
text: Hongkong, May 5.

label: text
text: (To the Editor of the China Mail.)

label: text
text: Sir,—If Cartlidge was beaten by Dupre he at least took his defeat like a gentleman. That much credit should be given him.

label: text
text: Dupre was also a sport and a gentleman as proved by his putting himself in the hands of British seconds and trainer. Thanks to them, he, in my opinion, won easily. Although he gave Carlidge every chance in the opening rounds, our lightweight champion never hurt him; but when the Frenchman hit, he certainly shook the C. P. O. Your correspondents should remember that Dupre has always fought first-class men of international repute whereas Carlidge has, as a rule, met Service men.

label: text
text: The public have heard how the verdict was arrived at. Dupre could afford to play with his man and he won by enough points to have given him the verdict. Your correspondents must have been influenced by Cartlidge's pro-roungement after the fight, anent wild swings and so on which were really scientific blows, propelled by an artist, and which found their mark more often than not.

label: text
text: FRONT RINGSIDE. Hongkong, May 5.

label: paragraph_title
text: $ ^{*} $ Bathing Scandal.

label: text
text: (2) the Editor of the China Mail).

label: text
text: Sir.—Is Repulse Bay a reserved beach or is it not? If it is, and I have been assured that it is on very good authority, what were cookies doing undressing themselves on the beach last Sunday about 5.45 p.m. prior to disporting themselves in the water?

label: text
text: It's a rotten thing to debar a fellow human being from the benefit of a cooling plunge, but the line must be drawn: somewhere and really the coolies, who came, I believe, from the different building operations progressing in the vicinity, were far from clean. Also, they are not the possessors of matsheds neither are there flocks behind which they can divest themselves of their clothing. On Sunday they were visible to many from the beach or matsheds and I think something ought to be done about it.

label: text
text: I understood that the beach was reserved and that the police were responsible to see that the restrictions were enforced. It would be rather a fiddling afternoon job for a police sergeant to be constantly on duty there but such scenes as were witnessed there last Sunday should be prevented from recurring somehow or other.

label: text
text: Yours, etc.,
